title: Plate Pouring Protocol
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.3yygpxw

steps.title: Prepare Hood and Plates
steps.instruction: Sterilize the hood with ethanol and organize the plates for pouring.

substeps.instruction: Sterilize the hood with ethanol.
Count the number of plates to be poured.
Stack plates inside the hood (stacks of 5 or 10 depending on convenience).

steps.title: Configure Hood and Pump Hardware
steps.instruction: Initialize the hood environment and connect the pump hardware.

substeps.instruction: Set the hood flow rate to 2.
Turn on the lights and plug in the switches.
Plug in the pump.

steps.title: Set Pump Parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the pump settings based on the plate size being used.

substeps.instruction: Set Volume: 45 mL for large plates (90mm), 15 mL for medium plates (60mm), or 3.5 mL for small plates (35mm).
Set Tube size: 8mm for large and medium plates, or 3mm for imaging (small) plates.
Set Direction to Clockwise.
Set Profile to Slow-Slow-Slow.

steps.title: Install and Prime Tubing
steps.instruction: Install the tubing and warm it to prevent agar solidification.

substeps.instruction: Place tubing around the pump clockwise, ensuring both ends are inserted into the agar bottle.
Prime the tubes (Setup -> Prime -> Accept) for a few minutes until tubes get warm; press Accept to stop.
Avoid touching the ends of the tube.

steps.title: Pour Agar into Plates
steps.instruction: Dispense the agar into the prepared plates using the foot pedal.

substeps.instruction: Place the nozzle perpendicularly on top of the center of the plate.
Press the foot pedal to allow agar to flow.
Wipe any agar spills from the surface with a paper towel after solidification.
If pausing for more than 1 minute, return the pump to prime mode.

steps.title: Manage Agar Bottles
steps.instruction: Transition between agar bottles to minimize waste.

substeps.instruction: When a bottle finishes, place the nozzle in a new bottle and prime to suck out residual agar.
Wash the empty bottle and fill it with hot water.
Put both openings into the new bottle and prime again.
Discard residual agar from the final bottle into the waste bucket.

steps.title: Clean and Store Equipment
steps.instruction: Clean the tubing and pump, and restore the hood workspace.

substeps.instruction: Wash tubing by priming hot water from a clean bottle to another to remove agar.
Prime air into the tubing to ensure no liquid remains.
Discard remaining agar in the waste bucket and wash bottles; place bottles in the grey box.
Close all hood switches and return the pump.
Clean the hood for the next user.
Wrap the tube in aluminium foil twice.
Label the foil with tube size and lab room number (e.g., 8mm Tubing R5020).
Place the tube in the autoclave basket in the media kitchen for collection the following day.

steps.title: Finalize Plates and Documentation
steps.instruction: Allow plates to set, label them, and record quality control data.

substeps.instruction: Let plates solidify under the hood for about an hour.
Label plates with the date poured.
Store plates upside down in the cold room.
Measure the weights of 3 random poured plates (with lids on) from the stack.
Enter weights into the plate weight data file in the shared folder.
Order agar in the media kitchen for the next pouring day (every other Monday).
